> ## James Walden withdraws from New York City's mayoral race
By
 Joseph Brusgard 
September 4, 2025 at 6:41 PM On September 2, 2025, independent New York City mayoral candidate James Walden (I) suspended his campaign for mayor. In an interview, Walden cited the rise of candidate Zohran Mamdani (D) as the factor for his withdrawal, saying, “The math is the math. And it doesn’t make sense for me to continue to push to surge, only to take ... safety, and improving affordability. Walden averaged 1% in polls showing a five-way contest. His campaign received the endorsement of former Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr. (D). Associated Press’ Jake Offenhartz wrote that Walden “had positioned himself as a free-market technocrat in ... contending with several familiar names.” In three polls conducted without Walden between Eric Adams (I), Mamdani (D), Curtis Sliwa (R), and Andrew Cuomo (I), Mamdani leads with an average of 36%, followed by Cuomo with 23%, Sliwa with 17%, and Adams with 10%. An average of 13% voters were undecided
